title_en: Xiajiajie Coal Mine, Maolan Town, Libo County, Qiannan Prefecture v. Zhang Xuexin and Guizhou Jiashenglong Group Mining Investment Co., Ltd. — dispute over third-party objection to execution
ruling_gist_en: The change of registration of the mining right holder upon payment of a deposit is a requirement of the merger and reorganization policy. The registered right holder paid only a deposit and did not actually operate the mining right. The applicant for enforcement should have been aware that the third party was the actual right holder of the mining right in question. Therefore, no protection of reliance interest arises from the registration of the mining right under the registered right holder's name. If the third party raises an enforcement objection, the people's court shall sustain it.
keywords_en: civil; action for enforcement objection; retrial; Supreme People's Court; Guizhou Province; legal person; natural person; Civil Procedure Law; Property Law; identification of actual right holder of mining right; protection of reliance interest in enforcement objection; conditions for revoking a ruling of debt satisfaction by property transfer; reversal of judgment; transfer of mining right; enforcement objection; debt satisfaction by property transfer; protection of reliance interest; application for retrial
full_text_en:
Guzhou Province Libo County Maolan Town Xiajiajie Coal Mine v. Zhang Xuexin, Guizhou Jiashenglong Group Mining Investment Co., Ltd. — dispute over an action for enforcement objection raised by a non-party

【Ruling Summary】

If the registration of the mining right owner is changed upon payment of the deposit, this is a requirement of the merger and reorganization policy. If the registered right holder only paid the deposit and did not actually operate, the applicant for enforcement should be aware that the non-party is the actual right holder of the mining right involved. The applicant for enforcement cannot claim reliance interest protection on the registration of the mining right in the name of the registered right holder. Where the non-party raises an enforcement objection, the people's court shall uphold it.

In an action for enforcement objection raised by a non-party, if the mining right involved has been transferred to the name of the applicant for enforcement by a ruling of debt satisfaction through property transfer before the judgment is rendered, when the people's court determines that the mining right shall not be enforced, if there are no issues such as maintaining the stability of judicial auction or sale procedures or protecting the interests of unspecified third parties, the scope of non-enforcement may extend to the said ruling of debt satisfaction through property transfer, and the ruling of debt satisfaction through property transfer shall be revoked, and compulsory enforcement measures such as seizure shall be lifted.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2021) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 141

Re-Applicant (Non-Party, Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Guizhou Province Libo County Maolan Town Xiajiajie Coal Mine, domiciled at Bijiu Village, Maolan Town, Libo County, Guizhou Province.

Managing Partner: Ou Dingjin, Mine Director of the Coal Mine.

Agent ad litem: Qin Jianbao, lawyer of Guangxi Xieyue Law Firm.

Respondent (Person Applying for Enforcement, Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Zhang Xuexin, male, born on October 1, 1967, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Duyun City, Guizhou Province.

Agent ad litem: Luo Haochang, lawyer of Guizhou Guida Law Firm.

Third Party (Person Subject to Enforcement): Guizhou Jiashenglong Group Mining Investment Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 66 West Jianshe Road, Yuping Town, Libo County, Guizhou Province.

Legal Representative: Ren Jianqu.

The re-applicant, Guizhou Province Libo County Maolan Town Xiajiajie Coal Mine (hereinafter referred to as Xiajiajie Coal Mine), filed a re-application with this Court against the Civil Judgment (2020) Qian Min Zhong No. 476 of the Guizhou High People's Court in connection with the dispute over the action for enforcement objection raised by a non-party with the respondent Zhang Xuexin and the third party Guizhou Jiashenglong Group Mining Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiashenglong Company). This Court, on May 12, 2021, rendered the Civil Ruling (2021) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 1484, granting the retrial of this case. This Lawfully formed a collegial panel and heard this case in open court. Ou Dingjin, the managing partner of the Xiajiajie Coal Mine (the re-applicant), and his agent ad litem Qin Jianbao, as well as Zhang Xuexin (the respondent) and his agent ad litem Luo Haochang, appeared in court for the hearing. The third party, Jiashenglong Company, did not appear in court without justifiable reason after being summoned by summons, so this Court proceeded with the hearing in its absence. The trial of this case is now concluded.

Xiajiajie Coal Mine applied for retrial on the grounds that: First, Xiajiajie Coal Mine is the actual right holder of the mining right known as "Xiajiajie Coal Mine (Ou Dingjin) in Maolan Town, Libo County, Guizhou Province" (i.e., the mining right involved in this case, certificate number C5200002012011120122487). The courts of first and second instance lacked evidence to prove that the mining right registered under the name of Jiashenglong Company and that the invalid mining license could be used to offset debts. The mining right involved was nominally attached to Jiashenglong Company, and there was a contractual agreement between Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company to this effect, and Jiashenglong Company also expressly stated that it had no objection. The "Enforcement Settlement Agreement" reached between Zhang Xuexin and Jiashenglong Company pertained to the ordinary monetary claim that Zhang Xuexin held against Jiashenglong Company. The "Agreement" signed between Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company on August 27, 2013, and the "Certificate of Confirmation of Property Rights" issued by Jiashenglong Company on September 26, 2014, stipulated the ownership of the mining right involved. Ownership should be protected in preference to claims. When Jiashenglong Company had only paid a deposit of RMB 1 million, the mining right involved was registered and transferred to its name, which was required under the merger and reorganization policy for coal mining enterprises in Guizhou Province. The mining right involved was not recorded within the scope of Jiashenglong Company's corporate property and did not belong to its assets. The Civil Judgment (2020) Qian 27 Min Zhong No. 225 had already rescinded the "Mining Rights and Equity Transfer Contract" and the "Supplementary Agreement Regarding the Mining Rights and Equity Transfer Contract" (hereinafter referred to as the Supplementary Agreement) signed between Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company. Both parties should return the property received from each other, and Jiashenglong Company had returned all the assets of the coal mine involved to Xiajiajie Coal Mine for management. Second, the mining right involved had already expired at the time of signing the "Enforcement Settlement Agreement," and the coal mine involved had been closed, so it could not be the subject of a contract transfer or debt satisfaction. The courts of first and second instance erred in the application of the law. Zhang Xuexin is a natural person and not a lawful mining enterprise, so he cannot be the transferee of a mining right. The Department of Natural Resources of Guizhou Province would not be able to register the transfer of the mining right to Zhang Xuexin, so the mining right involved could not be used for debt satisfaction in the enforcement proceedings. The auction of the mining right involved under the "Enforcement Settlement Agreement" without the approval of the Department of Natural Resources of Guizhou Province violated the relevant mandatory provisions of the Minerals Resources Law of the People's Republic of China and was invalid. In summary, Xiajiajie Coal Mine applied for retrial under Paragraphs (2) and (6) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, requesting the cancellation of the first and second instance judgments and a decision that the mining right involved shall not be enforced.

Zhang Xuexin argued in defense that: First, Xiajiajie Coal Mine does not have legitimate rights and interests in the mining right involved. The "Mining Right Transfer Contract for Xiajiajie Coal Mine (Merger and Reorganization) in Maolan Town, Libo County, Qiannan Prefecture" (hereinafter referred to as the Mining Right Transfer Contract) signed between Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company on August 27, 2013, stipulated that Xiajiajie Coal Mine would transfer the mining right involved to Jiashenglong Company by way of cooperation, with a transfer price of RMB 7 million. This transfer contract was approved by the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province, and the mining license was registered for change on November 27, 2013. Xiajiajie Coal Mine had thus lost the mining right involved. The old certificate held by Xiajiajie Coal Mine cannot prove that it is the owner of the mining right of the coal mine involved. The "Reply on the First Batch of Implementation Plans for the Merger and Reorganization of Coal Mining Enterprises of Jiashenglong Company" (Qian Mei Jian Bing Chong Zu Ban [2016] No. 2) did not confirm that after the closure of the coal mine involved, the ownership belonged to Xiajiajie Coal Mine. The "Work Plan for the Merger and Reorganization of Coal Mining Enterprises in Guizhou Province (Trial)" (Qian Fu Ban Fa [2012] No. 61) also did not provide that coal mining enterprises that were merged and reorganized could retain their property rights or mining rights. The above documents are not the basis for Xiajiajie Coal Mine to enjoy the ownership of the coal mine involved. The "Certificate of Confirmation of Property Rights," "Statement of Explanation," and "Declaration" submitted by Xiajiajie Coal Mine are self-statement materials of Jiashenglong Company or Xiajiajie Coal Mine, which do not comply with Article 46 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China and cannot prove that Xiajiajie Coal Mine has legitimate rights and interests in the coal mine involved. The "Mining Rights and Equity Transfer Contract" stipulated that if Jiashenglong Company delayed payment for more than one month, Xiajiajie Coal Mine had the right to rescind the contract. Xiajiajie Coal Mine filed a lawsuit for rescission on September 6, 2019, but its right of rescission had already been extinguished. The Civil Judgment (2020) Qian 27 Min Zhong No. 225 erred in the application of the law and cannot become a legitimate basis for Xiajiajie Coal Mine to enjoy the mining right involved. Second, the true purpose of the "Agreement" signed between Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company on August 27, 2013, was not to preserve the original mining rights and interests of the coal mine involved, but to address the risk of delayed payment of the transfer price that might arise from signing multiple transfer contracts. It cannot prove that Xiajiajie Coal Mine still enjoys the mining right involved. Whether Jiashenglong Company paid the transfer price as agreed is a matter of contractual debt and does not concern the ownership of the mining right involved. Third, in the situation where the coal mine involved was closed and the mining right involved had expired, Jiashenglong Company no longer had the right to use and benefit from the mineral resources of the coal mine involved. However, it still had property interests in the coal mine involved, and with the approval of the competent department of natural resources, the mining right could be sold to satisfy the debts of the mining enterprise or transferred to satisfy debts by property. Fourth, the "Enforcement Settlement Agreement" signed between Zhang Xuexin and Jiashenglong Company was legally valid, and this case had been fully enforced. Xiajiajie Coal Mine had lost the basis for its action. If Xiajiajie Coal Mine believed that the "Enforcement Settlement Agreement" was unlawful, it could apply to the enforcement court to confirm the validity of the agreement, but this should not be resolved in this case. Zhang Xuexin had transferred the claim of RMB 7 million that he held against Jiashenglong Company to Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine, and the enforcement court had changed the person applying for enforcement and had offset the debt by valuing the mining right of the coal mine involved at RMB 7 million. In summary, Zhang Xuexin requested the rejection of Xiajiajie Coal Mine's retrial application.

Jiashenglong Company submitted to this Court a "Statement on Materials Submitted for Retrial," stating that the total loan of RMB 14 million from Zhang Xuexin was unrelated to Xiajiajie Coal Mine.

Xiajiajie Coal Mine filed a lawsuit with the Qiannan Buyi and Miao Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance or Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate Court), requesting: 1. A decision that the already-closed Xiajiajie Coal Mine and the expired mining right of Xiajiajie Coal Mine (certificate number C5200002012011120122487, i.e., the mining right involved) shall not be seized or auctioned to offset Zhang Xuexin's debts; 2. The litigation costs of this case be borne by Zhang Xuexin.

The court of first instance found the following facts: In accordance with the implementation plan for the merger and reorganization of coal mining enterprises in Guizhou Province, on July 30, 2013, and August 27, 2013, Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company successively signed the "Mining Rights and Equity Transfer Contract" and the "Supplementary Agreement," agreeing to transfer the mining right involved, and also agreeing on the term, transfer amount, and equity shares. On August 27, 2013, Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company signed an "Agreement," which stated that the parties had entered the stage of changing the mining right transaction in the course of the merger and reorganization of coal mining enterprises, and they reached an agreement on the issue that Jiashenglong Company was temporarily unable to pay the transfer price for the acquired coal mine. The agreement stipulated that the signed coal mine acquisition contract would continue to be effective, and the signed "Mining Right Transfer Contract" would be used for the purpose of handling the merger and reorganization of the coal mine's mining right and would not serve as the true basis for payment in the mining right transaction. On November 20, 2013, Jiashenglong Company obtained a mining license (certificate number C5200002012011120122487), which indicated that the mining right owner was Jiashenglong Company and the mine name was "Guizhou Jiashenglong Group Mining Investment Co., Ltd. Xiajiajie Coal Mine, Maolan Town, Libo County" (i.e., the coal mine involved). On March 4, 2016, the Office of the Leading Group for the Merger and Reorganization of Coal Mining Enterprises in Guizhou Province and the Energy Bureau of Guizhou Province jointly issued Document No. Qian Mei Jian Bing Chong Zu Ban [2016] No. 2, deciding to close the coal mine involved.

It was also found that, in connection with the dispute over private lending between Zhang Xuexin and Jiashenglong Company, the Guizhou High People's Court rendered the Civil Judgment (2017) Qian Min Zhong No. 128, ordering Jiashenglong Company to repay Zhang Xuexin a loan of RMB 11.28 million and interest (calculated from December 4, 2014, until the repayment of principal and interest, at an annual rate of 24%). As Jiashenglong Company failed to perform the obligations under the effective judgment, Zhang Xuexin applied to the court of first instance for compulsory enforcement. During the enforcement proceedings, the court of first instance inquired with the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province about the mining rights held by Jiashenglong Company. On May 28, 2018, the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province's inquiry results showed that: As of that date, a total of 16 valid mining rights, including the mining right involved, were registered under the name of Jiashenglong Company, and there was no valid mortgage record for the mining right involved at the Department. Based on the above inquiry results, the court of first instance seized some of the mining rights under the name of Jiashenglong Company, including the mining right involved. Xiajiajie Coal Mine, claiming to be the actual right holder of the mining right involved, objected to the court of first instance, requesting the suspension of enforcement of the mining right involved. The court of first instance held that the registered right holder of the mining right involved was Jiashenglong Company, not Xiajiajie Coal Mine, and therefore dismissed the enforcement objection raised by Xiajiajie Coal Mine.

It was further found that the inquiry results from the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province also showed that the validity period of the mining right involved registered by Jiashenglong Company at the Department was until June 2018.

It was also found that, in the enforcement proceedings of the private lending dispute between Zhang Xuexin and Jiashenglong Company, Zhang Xuexin and Jiashenglong Company entered into an "Enforcement Settlement Agreement," in which Jiashenglong Company agreed to provide the coal mine involved, which belonged to it, as security and for seizure.

On December 12, 2019, the court of first instance rendered the Civil Judgment (2019) Qian 27 Min Chu No. 122: Dismissing the claims of Xiajiajie Coal Mine. The case acceptance fee was RMB 60,800, to be borne by Xiajiajie Coal Mine.

Xiajiajie Coal Mine was dissatisfied with the first instance judgment and appealed, requesting: 1. To overturn the first instance judgment and instead decide that the already-closed Xiajiajie Coal Mine and the expired mining right involved (certificate number C5200002012011120122487) shall not be seized or auctioned to offset Zhang Xuexin's debt of RMB 7 million; 2. The litigation costs of this case be borne by Zhang Xuexin.

The facts found by the court of second instance were basically consistent with those found by the court of first instance. During the second instance proceedings, Xiajiajie Coal Mine submitted another effective civil judgment, namely the Civil Judgment (2020) Qian 27 Min Zhong No. 225 of the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate Court, which rescinded the "Mining Rights and Equity Transfer Contract" signed between Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company on July 30, 2013, and the "Supplementary Agreement" signed on August 27, 2013. Xiajiajie Coal Mine intended to use this effective judgment to prove that the mining right involved belonged to it and that the "Enforcement Settlement Agreement" signed between Zhang Xuexin and Jiashenglong Company was invalid. Zhang Xuexin, in his cross-examination, argued that this effective judgment could not achieve Xiajiajie Coal Mine's purpose of proof. Jiashenglong Company acknowledged the authenticity of this effective judgment.

The court of second instance held that the key to whether the claims raised by Xiajiajie Coal Mine in this case could be established was whether it was the lawful owner of the mining right of the coal mine involved or whether it enjoyed other lawful civil rights and interests sufficient to exclude the compulsory enforcement of the mining right involved.

According to Paragraph 6 of Article 6 of the Implementing Regulations of the Minerals Resources Law of the People's Republic of China, a unit or individual that obtains a mining license is called a mining right owner. In this case, although the mining right involved once belonged to Xiajiajie Coal Mine, during the period of coal mine merger and reorganization in Guizhou Province, Xiajiajie Coal Mine, in accordance with the merger and reorganization policy and relevant legal provisions, reported the mining right involved for administrative approval and had it registered and transferred to the name of Jiashenglong Company. Jiashenglong Company had thereby lawfully obtained a mining license and became the statutory mining right owner of the coal mine involved. Xiajiajie Coal Mine was no longer the statutory mining right owner of the coal mine involved by law. A mining right is a特许 right obtained through administrative approval to exploit mineral resources, which is different from ordinary property rights. The claim of Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company that the mining right involved was held under a nominal attachment arrangement and that Xiajiajie Coal Mine remained the actual mining right owner of the coal mine involved lacks legal basis and cannot negate the mining license lawfully issued by the administrative authority to Jiashenglong Company. Although the effective judgment of another case submitted by Xiajiajie Coal Mine in the second instance rescinded the aforementioned transfer contract between Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company, it did not and could not decide that the mining right owner of the coal mine involved was Xiajiajie Coal Mine; otherwise, it would be substituting judicial power for administrative power, thereby violating the provisions of mineral resources laws and regulations. After the contract between Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company was rescinded by the judgment, Xiajiajie Coal Mine could lawfully enjoy a corresponding contractual claim against Jiashenglong Company, but it did not directly obtain the mining right involved by law. In fact, according to the current mineral resources management regulations in China, the owner of a coal resource mining right should be a legal person and meet other specific conditions. Under the principle of equal priority of claims, the contractual claim that Xiajiajie Coal Mine might enjoy against Jiashenglong Company based on the rescission of the contract cannot override the claim determined by an effective judgment that Zhang Xuexin holds against Jiashenglong Company, nor can it preclude the enforcement court from enforcing the mining right under Jiashenglong Company's name based on Zhang Xuexin's application. When the enforcement court seized the mining right involved under Jiashenglong Company's name, the mining license involved had not been lawfully cancelled or revoked by the administrative authority; rather, the mine needed to be merged and reorganized with other coal mines under Jiashenglong Company's name. The seized mining right had corresponding property value. During the implementation of the merger and reorganization policy for coal mining enterprises in Guizhou Province, the handling of related coal mine mining rights had its particularity. The expiration of the mining license of the coal mine involved did not mean the automatic extinction of the mining right, and the administrative authority had not determined that the mining right had been extinguished. The closure of the coal mine involved due to merger and reorganization also cannot negate the realizable value of the existing mining right of the mine through merger and reorganization. The other grounds of appeal raised by Xiajiajie Coal Mine all fail to prove that it is the statutory mining right owner of the seized mining right involved, nor can they prove that it enjoys a priority over Zhang Xuexin's claim against Jiashenglong Company with respect to the mining right involved. Therefore, Xiajiajie Coal Mine's grounds of appeal regarding the exclusion of enforcement of the mining right involved cannot be sustained.

In summary, on August 3, 2020, the court of second instance rendered the Civil Judgment (2020) Qian Min Zhong No. 476: Dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. The second instance case acceptance fee was RMB 60,800, to be borne by Xiajiajie Coal Mine.

To fully consider the allegations and defenses of all parties based on the evidence, this Court reviewed the evidence submitted by each party in different trial proceedings.

Xiajiajie Coal Mine submitted the following evidence to the courts of first and second instance:

Evidence 1: The Enforcement Ruling (2019) Qian 27 Zhi Yi No. 54 of the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate Court, which is the basis for Xiajiajie Coal Mine to file the action for enforcement objection by a non-party.

Evidence 2-4: The "Work Plan for the Merger and Reorganization of Coal Mining Enterprises in Guizhou Province (Trial)" (Qian Fu Ban Fa [2012] No. 61) issued by the General Office of the Guizhou Provincial People's Government; the "Reply on the First Batch of Implementation Plans for the Merger and Reorganization of Coal Mining Enterprises of Guizhou Jiashenglong Group Mining Investment Co., Ltd." (Qian Mei Jian Bing Chong Zu Ban [2016] No. 2) jointly issued by the Office of the Leading Group for the Merger and Reorganization of Coal Mining Enterprises in Guizhou Province and the Energy Bureau of Guizhou Province; and the "Notice on Printing and Distributing the Implementation Plan for Eliminating Backward Production Capacity and Accelerating Transformation and Upgrading of the Coal Industry in Libo County" (Li Dang Ban Fa [2018] No. 35) jointly issued by the Office of the CPC Libo County Committee and the Office of the People's Government of Libo County. The purpose was to prove that the coal mine involved was integrated and reorganized according to government requirements, as a result of government action; that the mining right involved was only nominally attached to Jiashenglong Company; and that although the coal mine involved had been closed, the legal personality of Xiajiajie Coal Mine still existed, and the coal mine involved should not be auctioned to satisfy debts.

Evidence 5: The "Mining Rights and Equity Transfer Contract," "Supplementary Agreement," and "Agreement" signed between Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company. The purpose was to prove that Jiashenglong Company did not pay the transfer price for the coal mine involved to Xiajiajie Coal Mine as agreed, and that the merger and reorganization between the parties was merely formal.

Evidence 6-8: The mining license (Certificate No. C5200002012011120122487) issued by the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province to Jia Shenglong Company, valid from November 2013 to June 2018, with the mining right holder being Jia Shenglong Company; the mining license (Certificate No. C5200002012011120122487) issued by the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province to Xiajiajie Coal Mine, valid from December 2011 to June 2018, with the mining right holder being Xiajiajie Coal Mine; the announcement published by the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court on its online platform on August 27, 2019, regarding the auction of the mining right involved in the case under the name of Jia Shenglong Company. Intended to prove that the mining license stipulated in the "Enforcement Settlement Agreement" reached between Zhang Xuexin and Jia Shenglong Company was the mining license under the name of Jia Shenglong Company as the mining right holder, not the mining license under the name of Xiajiajie Coal Mine; moreover, at the time of auction, the mining right involved in the case had already expired, and the court's auction was erroneous.

Evidence 9-11: The "Certificate of Confirmation of Property Rights" issued by Jia Shenglong Company on September 26, 2014; the "Statement of Facts" issued by Xiajiajie Coal Mine on September 18, 2019, stamped for confirmation by the Libo County Emergency Management Bureau; the "Declaration" issued by Jia Shenglong Company to the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court on September 3, 2019. Intended to prove that Jia Shenglong Company and Xiajiajie Coal Mine jointly confirmed that Xiajiajie Coal Mine was the actual right holder of the mining right involved in the case, and that the Libo County Emergency Management Bureau was also aware of this fact.

Evidence 12-13: The "Enterprise Credit Information Publicity Report" concerning Jia Shenglong Company from the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; the "Partnership Business License" and "Organization Code Certificate" of Xiajiajie Coal Mine. Intended to prove that the主体 qualification of the coal mine involved in the case is still Xiajiajie Coal Mine, and that Xiajiajie Coal Mine is the actual right holder of the mining right involved in the case.

Evidence 14: The "Enforcement Settlement Agreement" signed between Zhang Xuexin and Jia Shenglong Company during the enforcement proceedings of the effective judgment in their private lending dispute. Intended to prove that Zhang Xuexin, as an individual, was not a qualified party to sign the agreement, and that auctioning an already expired mining license involved in the case to repay the debt violated relevant legal provisions and should be null and void.

Evidence 15: The Civil Judgment (2020) Qian 27 Min Zhong No. 225 of the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2019) Qian 2722 Min Chu No. 1656 of the Libo County People's Court. Intended to prove that the effective judgment had already rescinded the "Mining Right and Equity Transfer Contract" and its "Supplemental Agreement" between Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jia Shenglong Company, and that the mining right involved in the case belongs to Xiajiajie Coal Mine.

During the trial of this case in the first-instance court on November 25, 2019, Zhang Xuexin did not raise any objection to the authenticity of the above evidence. When questioned by this court on April 14, 2021, Zhang Xuexin first clearly stated that he had no objection to the authenticity of the above evidence, but later claimed that he had objections to the authenticity of Evidence 9-11, arguing that they were evidence subsequently supplemented by Xiajiajie Coal Mine. During the public hearing of this case on July 26, 2021, Zhang Xuexin raised objections to the authenticity of Evidence 9-11 but did not submit any rebuttal evidence. This court admits Evidence 9-11.

Zhang Xuexin submitted the following new evidence to this court:

Evidence 1: "Archival Materials of Xiajiajie Coal Mine" (copy). Intended to prove that Xiajiajie Coal Mine transferred the mining right involved in the case due to the merger and reorganization policy for coal mining enterprises in Guizhou Province; the right holder of the mining right involved in the case had been changed from Xiajiajie Coal Mine to Jia Shenglong Company; Xiajiajie Coal Mine does not have legitimate rights and interests in the mining right involved in the case. This evidence was obtained by Zhang Xuexin after he applied to this court for investigation and evidence collection before the retrial hearing. After this court communicated with Xiajiajie Coal Mine, Xiajiajie Coal Mine obtained the above evidence from the Department of Natural Resources of Guizhou Province and provided it to Zhang Xuexin.

Evidence 2-5: The "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhang Xuexin and Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine on December 6, 2019; the "Application for Change of Applying Enforcement Creditor" and "Application for Debt Repayment by Transfer of Property" submitted by Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine to the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court on December 6, 2019; the Enforcement Ruling (2019) Qian 27 Zhi Hui 9-5 of the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court. Intended to prove that Zhang Xuexin had transferred the RMB 7 million creditor's rights involved in the case to Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine, and that the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court had ruled to transfer the mining right involved in the case to Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine in lieu of debt.

Evidence 6-7: The Assistance Enforcement Notice (2018) Qian 27 Zhi 8-6 of the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court; the reply letter from the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province dated May 28, 2018, regarding the registration and filing of the seizure and mortgage of the mining right involved in the case. Intended to prove that the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court had issued an assistance enforcement notice to the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province, and that the mining right involved in the case had been seized through lawful procedures.

Evidence 8-10: The "Investigation and Evaluation Report on the Current Situation of the Mine Geological Environment of Xiajiajie Coal Mine in Maolan Town, Libo County" issued by Xiajiajie Coal Mine in December 2019; comparative diagrams of the mine geological environment before and after restoration of Xiajiajie Coal Mine; the "Letter of Entrustment on Implementation of the Restoration and Management Work of the Mine Geological Environment of Xiajiajie Coal Mine in Maolan Town, Libo County" issued by the Libo County Bureau of Natural Resources on November 26, 2019. Intended to prove that the Libo County People's Government had carried out environmental restoration (reclamation and re-greening) on the coal mine involved in the case, and that Xiajiajie Coal Mine's claim that it had taken over the assets of the coal mine involved in the case in accordance with the Civil Judgment (2020) Qian 27 Min Zhong No. 225 of the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court was untrue.

Evidence 11-13: The "Approval on the Implementation Plan for the Mergers and Reorganizations of Panzhou Coal Development Corporation (Fourth Batch)" (Qian Mei Zhuan Xing Sheng Ji Ban [2019] No. 99) issued by the Guizhou Province Leading Group Office for Eliminating Backward Production Capacity and Accelerating Transformation and Upgrading in the Coal Industry on December 31, 2019; the minutes of the 16th meeting of the Guizhou Province Leading Group Office for Eliminating Backward Production Capacity and Accelerating Transformation and Upgrading in the Coal Industry ([2019]); the mining license with the mine name "Guizhou Yi Shenglong Mining Co., Ltd. Libo County Maolan Town Fuqi Coal Mine" issued by the Department of Natural Resources of Guizhou Province on May 7, 2021. Intended to prove that, with the approval of the Guizhou Province Leading Group Office for Eliminating Backward Production Capacity and Accelerating Transformation and Upgrading in the Coal Industry, the coal mine involved in the case was included in the fourth batch of mergers and closures of mines of Guizhou Yi Shenglong Mining Co., Ltd. Libo County Maolan Town Fuqi Coal Mine; the execution procedures concerning the coal mine involved in the case had been completed, and Xiajiajie Coal Mine had lost the basis for its claim.

Xiajiajie Coal Mine did not raise any objection to the authenticity of the above evidence but argued that the transfer of creditor's rights did not comply with legal provisions, the change of the enforcement debtor was illegal, and the relevant government departments had determined that the mining right involved in the case belongs to Xiajiajie Coal Mine.

Jia Shenglong Company submitted the following new evidence to this court:

Evidence 1: The "Notice on the Appointment of Comrade Zhang Xuexin" (copy) issued by Jia Shenglong Company on September 1, 2013, and the "Explanation of the Circumstances of the 'Notice on the Appointment of Comrade Zhang Xuexin'" (original) issued by Jia Shenglong Company on July 24, 2021. Intended to prove that Jia Shenglong Company appointed Zhang Xuexin as its Deputy General Manager, responsible for the company's financing and integration of coal mine resources; the original appointment notice was kept in the personal safe of Cao Lebo, the former legal representative of Jia Shenglong Company, and because Cao Lebo is currently detained in Jinsha County Detention Center, the original cannot be provided.

Evidence 2: Bank account statements and related vouchers of Jia Shenglong Company at branches including China Construction Bank Corporation Guiyang Dongshan Sub-branch and Bank of Guiyang Co., Ltd. Duyun Sub-branch. Intended to prove that Zhang Xuexin, through the above accounts of Jia Shenglong Company under his control, transferred RMB 16,325,000 from funds remitted to Jia Shenglong Company by other coal mines into his personal account.

Evidence 3: The Civil Judgment (2017) Qian Min Zhong No. 128 of the Guizhou High People's Court. Intended to prove that Zhang Xuexin had transferred RMB 16,325,000 from the accounts of Jia Shenglong Company into his own account, but that judgment did not determine that this sum constituted loan repayment.

Evidence 4: The "Contract for the Transfer of Mining Right and Equity of Duoyuyan Coal Mine in Luobang Town, Duyun City" and its "Supplemental Agreement," the "Contract for the Transfer of Mining Right and Equity of Jidang Coal Mine in Shuiyao Township, Libo County" and its "Supplemental Agreement," the "China Construction Bank Customer Special Voucher," etc. Intended to prove that Zhang Xuexin transferred the Duoyuyan Coal Mine and Jidang Coal Mine, both under the name of Jia Shenglong Company, to Guizhou Yongji Mining Investment Co., Ltd., and directed the corresponding transfer payments to bank accounts controlled by Zhang Xuexin.

Evidence 5: The "Payment Application" issued by Jia Shenglong Company to Guizhou Luzhong Mining Co., Ltd. on September 23, 2014, requesting payment to Zhang Xuexin's account, and the "Receipt" issued by Zhang Xuexin. Intended to prove that Zhang Xuexin instructed Guizhou Luzhong Mining Co., Ltd. to transfer the transfer proceeds into Zhang Xuexin's account.

Evidence 6: The Civil Ruling (2016) Qian 0115 Min Chu No. 330 of the Guanshanhu District People's Court of Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, and the corresponding Complaint, Application for Withdrawal of Lawsuit, and Certificate issued by Jia Shenglong Company. Intended to prove that Zhang Xuexin forged the company seal of Jia Shenglong Company and the signature of its then legal representative, Cao Lebo, and sued Guizhou Luzhong Mining Co., Ltd. for payment of the remaining transfer price; this was discovered by Jia Shenglong Company, which issued a written certificate to the court, leading to the civil case being ruled to allow the withdrawal of the lawsuit.

Zhang Xuexin did not recognize the authenticity, legality, or relevance of the above Evidence 1, and had no objection to the authenticity or legality of Evidence 2-6 but argued that they were irrelevant to this case and could not achieve the intended purpose of proof.

Xiajiajie Coal Mine recognized the authenticity, legality, and relevance of Evidence 1-6.

For evidence whose authenticity is recognized by the parties, this court admits it. For evidence to which a party has raised objections and the question of whether the matters intended to be proven are established, this court will analyze and discuss them in the part of the judgment concerning the facts found.

Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Zhang Xuexin have no objection to the facts found by the first-instance and second-instance courts. Upon review, this court confirms them. Based on the evidence submitted by the parties in the first-instance and second-instance proceedings, the new evidence submitted to this court, and the statements of the parties, this court additionally finds the following:

I. Regarding the merger and reorganization of coal mining enterprises in Guizhou Province and the transfer of the mining right involved in the case

The "Work Plan for the Merger and Reorganization of Coal Mining Enterprises in Guizhou Province (Trial)" issued by the General Office of the People's Government of Guizhou Province on December 19, 2012, states the following: to ... actively and steadily promote the merger and reorganization of coal mining enterprises throughout the province, deepen the integration of coal mines, orderly develop coal resources, optimize the coal industry structure, and promote the sustained, healthy, and safe development of the province's coal industry, this Work Plan is formulated; to promote the merger and reorganization of coal mining enterprises through policy guidance and government promotion, in accordance with relevant laws and regulations; after the implementation plan is approved, the people's governments at the city (prefecture), county (city, district, special district) levels shall organize and coordinate, the merging and reorganizing entities shall implement specifically, and the merger and reorganization work shall be basically completed by March 31, 2014; after the merger and reorganization, all types of certificates and licenses of the coal mines must be changed to the name of the merging and reorganizing entity.

The "Approval on the Implementation Plan for the Merger and Reorganization of Coal Mining Enterprises of Jia Shenglong Company (First Batch)" jointly issued by the Office of the Leading Group for the Merger and Reorganization of Coal Mining Enterprises in Guizhou Province and the Energy Bureau of Guizhou Province on March 4, 2016, was made in response to a request from Jia Shenglong Company. The approval includes the retention of Jia Shenglong Company's Fuqi Coal Mine in Maolan Town, Libo County, and the closure of Jia Shenglong Company's Xiajiajie Coal Mine in Maolan Town, Libo County.

On July 30, 2013, Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jia Shenglong Company signed the "Mining Right and Equity Transfer Contract," which states: the name of the mining right to be transferred is the Xiajiajie Coal Mine (Ou Dingjin) in Maolan Town, Libo County, Qiannan Prefecture; the mining license number is C5200002012011120122487; the total consideration for all assets is RMB 30 million; Jia Shenglong Company acquires 99% equity of Xiajiajie Coal Mine for a price of RMB 29.7 million; when the name change is signed at the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province, Jia Shenglong Company shall pay RMB 1 million as a deposit for performance of the contract. On August 27, 2013, Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jia Shenglong Company signed a "Supplemental Agreement," amending the total consideration to RMB 38 million for all assets; Jia Shenglong Company acquires 99% of the shares of Xiajiajie Coal Mine for a price of RMB 37.62 million; the payment conditions and amount of the deposit were not changed. On February 10, 2014, Jia Shenglong Company paid RMB 1 million to Xiajiajie Coal Mine as transfer consideration.

On August 27, 2013, Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jia Shenglong Company signed the "Mining Right Transfer Contract," which stipulates that the mining right of the coal mine involved in the case is to be transferred to Jia Shenglong Company by way of joint venture or cooperation, with the transfer consideration being RMB 7 million; after the transfer, Xiajiajie Coal Mine holds 49% of the mining right, and Jia Shenglong Company holds 51%; within three working days after signing the contract, Jia Shenglong Company shall pay RMB 500,000; after six months, it shall pay RMB 4 million; the remaining RMB 2.5 million shall be paid after the certificates and licenses are changed and completed; only after Jia Shenglong Company has paid the full transfer consideration to Xiajiajie Coal Mine in accordance with the contract may it request Xiajiajie Coal Mine to provide all required materials such as the mining license; Xiajiajie Coal Mine is obligated to assist Jia Shenglong Company in handling the registration of the mining license change and related procedures. This "Mining Right Transfer Contract" was the contract filed with the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province.

On August 27, 2013, Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jia Shenglong Company signed an "Agreement," Article 2 of which stipulates that the "Mining Right Transfer Contract" signed as required by the Provincial Department of Land and Resources is to be used solely for the purpose of handling the merger and reorganization of the coal mine's mining right and shall not serve as the actual basis for the payment of the mining right transaction price.

On September 26, 2014, Jia Shenglong Company issued a "Certificate of Confirmation of Property Rights" to Xiajiajie Coal Mine, undertaking that until Jia Shenglong Company has paid all mining right consideration, all property rights of the coal mine involved in the case (including the mining right and all property rights on the surface of the coal mine, etc.) remain owned by Libo County Maolan Town Xiajiajie Coal Mine (legal representative: Ou Dingjin). On September 18, 2019, Xiajiajie Coal Mine issued a "Statement of Facts" stating that on September 4, 2018, Jia Shenglong Company, Libo County Maolan Town Fuqi Coal Mine, and Xiajiajie Coal Mine conducted mediation at the Libo County Emergency Management Bureau regarding compensation for the withdrawal of property rights. The Libo County Emergency Management Bureau noted "the facts are true" on the "Statement of Facts" and affixed its seal. On September 3, 2019, Jia Shenglong Company issued a "Declaration" to the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court stating that, in accordance with the spirit of the provincial government's requirements for coal mine merger and reorganization, and in compliance with the demand to establish group companies for coal mines in various counties of the province, the original coal mining enterprises were required to merge and reorganize into group companies. To assist Jia Shenglong Company in handling the relevant certificate procedures, Xiajiajie Coal Mine entered Jia Shenglong Company for merger and reorganization. On August 27, 2013, Jia Shenglong Company and Xiajiajie Coal Mine (legal representative: Ou Dingjin) signed a "Coal Mine Acquisition Agreement." However, after the mining right registration procedures were changed, Jia Shenglong Company was unable to perform the "Coal Mine Acquisition Agreement" and has not paid the mining right transfer consideration on time to date. Therefore, all property rights of the coal mine involved in the case belong to Qiannan Libo County Maolan Town Xiajiajie Coal Mine, and no other entity or individual has the right to dispose of any property rights of Xiajiajie Coal Mine.

After the mining right involved in the case was registered and changed to the name of Jia Shenglong Company, the coal mine remained in a state of closure and suspension of operations. Jia Shenglong Company did not actually operate the coal mine involved in the case. By an approval of the Guizhou Province Leading Group Office for Eliminating Backward Production Capacity and Accelerating Transformation and Upgrading in the Coal Industry on December 31, 2019, the coal mine involved in the case was closed.

II. Regarding the private lending dispute case between Zhang Xuexin and Jia Shenglong Company

The Civil Judgment (2017) Qian Min Zhong No. 128 of the Guizhou High People's Court found the following facts: "After Jia Shenglong Company was incorporated on January 5, 2013, the company's legal representative, Cao Lebo, authorized and appointed Zhang Xuexin, in the name of the company, to exercise all rights that the company, as the investor of the acquired coal mines, was entitled to, including but not limited to: the right to transfer the mining right externally, the right to transfer the coal mine externally, and the right to collect transfer proceeds. The two seals affixed to the bank account at Bank of Guiyang and the account at China Construction Bank opened by Jia Shenglong Company for this purpose, in addition to the company's financial seal, one seal was Zhang Xuexin's personal seal. The use of funds in the above two bank accounts of Jia Shenglong Company required Zhang Xuexin's consent." Zhang Xuexin has no objection to the above facts themselves but claims that he did not participate in the transaction of the mining right involved in the case.

According to the facts found in the Civil Judgment (2017) Qian Min Zhong No. 128 of the Guizhou High People's Court, Zhang Xuexin, in that case, sought the return of loan principal of RMB 14 million from Jia Shenglong Company, which he had transferred in multiple installments to the account of Jia Shenglong Company from September to October 2013.

During the hearing of this case in this court, Zhang Xuexin acknowledged that before lending the above funds to Jia Shenglong Company, he did not check the mining right under the name of Jia Shenglong Company at the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province, nor did he establish any security interest over the mining right involved in the case.

During the pre-trial meeting and the hearing of this case held by this court on July 26, 2021, Zhang Xuexin stated that the mining right involved in the case had already been transferred to Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine on May 7, 2021, through the enforcement procedures of the enforcement court; the enforcement court transferred RMB 3 million to Zhang Xuexin via bank transfer; Xiajiajie Coal Mine no longer had any litigable interest in the mining right involved in the case. Xiajiajie Coal Mine expressed its opinion on this matter, stating that an expired mining license cannot be changed; before the hearing, it had obtained the archives of the mining right involved in the case from the Department of Natural Resources of Guizhou Province, and those archives contained no record that the mining right involved in the case had been registered and changed to the name of Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine. Upon examination, during the enforcement proceedings of the Civil Judgment (2017) Qian Min Zhong No. 128 of the Guizhou High People's Court, Zhang Xuexin and Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine entered into a "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" on December 6, 2019, regarding the loan principal of RMB 7 million specified in the judgment; on December 6, 2019, Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine submitted to the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court the "Application for Change of Applying Enforcement Creditor" and the "Application for Debt Repayment by Transfer of Property," requesting a ruling that the mining right of the coal mine involved in the case be deemed as belonging to Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine at the second auction's flow price; with Zhang Xuexin providing enforcement guarantees, the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court issued the Enforcement Ruling (2019) Qian 27 Zhi Hui 9-5 on December 8, 2019, ruling to change Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine to be one of the applying enforcement creditors in this case and to deliver the mining right involved in the case, valued at RMB 7 million, to Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine in satisfaction of a debt of RMB 7 million.

III. Other Circumstances

Jia Shenglong Company submitted to this court the bank account statements and related vouchers (i.e., Evidence 2) for its accounts at China Construction Bank Corporation Guiyang Dongshan Sub-branch and Bank of Guiyang Co., Ltd. Duyun Sub-branch. Zhang Xuexin has no objection to the authenticity of this evidence. Upon examination, the relevant vouchers are bank telegraphic transfer vouchers or instant payment vouchers, etc., with the remitter being Jia Shenglong Company and the payee being Zhang Xuexin; the bank voucher copies or debit voucher copies from the remitting bank bear both the financial seal of Jia Shenglong Company and the personal seal of Zhang Xuexin; the earliest transaction date was October 15, 2013, and the latest was October 11, 2016.

Jiashenglong Company submitted to this court a "Notice on the Appointment of Comrade Zhang Xuexin" (copy) issued on September 1, 2013 to all departments and coal mines of the group, and a "Statement on the 'Notice on the Appointment of Comrade Zhang Xuexin'" (original) issued by Jiashenglong Company on July 24, 2021, both bearing the seal of Jiashenglong Company. The aforesaid appointment notice stated, "After research and decision by the shareholders' meeting of the group company, Comrade Zhang Xuexin is appointed as Deputy General Manager of the group company, responsible for financing and integration of coal mine resources." The aforesaid statement stated, "The original of this appointment notice is archived in the personal safe of Cao Lebai, the former legal representative of the group company. Cao Lebai is currently detained in Jinsha County Detention Center, and the original cannot be produced, but Zhang Xuexin was indeed appointed as Deputy General Manager by our group company." Although Zhang Xuexin disputed the authenticity of this appointment notice and statement, in light of the relevant facts found in the civil judgment (2017) Qian Min Zhong No. 128 of the Guizhou High People's Court and the fact that the bank transfer vouchers from Jiashenglong Company to Zhang Xuexin simultaneously bore the financial seal of Jiashenglong Company and the private seal of Zhang Xuexin, and Zhang Xuexin failed to provide evidence sufficient to overturn the appointment notice and statement, it can be determined that Jiashenglong Company's claim that it appointed Zhang Xuexin as its Deputy General Manager responsible for financing and integrating coal mine resources is established. Even if it cannot be determined that Jiashenglong Company appointed Zhang Xuexin as its Deputy General Manager, it can at least be determined that Zhang Xuexin was responsible for Jiashenglong Company's external acquisition of coal mines, transfer of coal mines, and payment of coal mine transfer prices since September 2013.

During the questioning of the parties in the retrial application procedure of this court, Zhang Xuexin stated that he understood the coal mine enterprise merger and reorganization policy of Guizhou Province. During the pre-trial meeting organized by this court in the retrial procedure, he stated that before the implementation of the coal mine enterprise merger and reorganization policy of Guizhou Province, he also operated small coal mines, and one of his coal mines had been merged and reorganized under the name of Jiashenglong Company. Jiashenglong Company did not pay the transfer price, and he filed a lawsuit requesting the return of the coal mine and obtained support.

In the retrial, this court holds that the focus of the dispute in this case is whether Xiajiajie Coal Mine has a civil right and interest in the mining right involved in the case sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement. This requires consideration of two issues: first, whether Xiajiajie Coal Mine is the actual right holder of the mining right involved in the case; second, whether the civil right and interest of Xiajiajie Coal Mine in the mining right involved in the case is sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement, i.e., whether the civil right and interest of Xiajiajie Coal Mine in the mining right involved in the case has priority over the creditor's right enjoyed by Zhang Xuexin based on the enforcement basis.

I. Whether Xiajiajie Coal Mine is the actual right holder of the mining right involved in the case

Although the mining right is a right generated based on administrative licensing, the exploitation and utilization of mineral products itself is a type of usufructuary right, belonging to the category of real rights. In the utilization of the right after the initial establishment of the mining right, i.e., the administrative licensing registration, there exists in practice a situation where the nominal right holder and the actual right holder are separated. Article 33 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If a dispute arises over the ownership or content of a real right, an interested person may request confirmation of the right." When a dispute arises between the nominal right holder and the actual right holder over the ownership of the mining right, requesting confirmation of the actual right holder through an action for execution objection conforms to the purpose of civil litigation. What needs to be clarified is that the people's court, in an action for execution objection, confirms the actual right status of the mining right, not the administrative licensing of the mining right, and does not have the direct effect of producing licensing registration. After the people's court confirms the actual right holder of the mining right, whether the actual right holder can obtain the mining right still depends on whether it meets the other conditions of administrative regulations regarding licensing registration of mining rights.

In this case, based on the facts found above, it can be determined that Xiajiajie Coal Mine is the actual right holder of the mining right involved in the case. The reasons are as follows:

First, the change of the mining right involved in the case to the name of Jiashenglong Company was carried out in accordance with the requirements of the Guizhou Province coal mine enterprise merger and reorganization policy, and was not the true intention of Xiajiajie Coal Mine. Although Jiashenglong Company and Xiajiajie Coal Mine signed the "Mining Right Equity Transfer Contract" and the "Supplemental Agreement," the transaction was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the Guizhou Province coal mine enterprise merger and reorganization policy, differing from a transfer contract reached through free negotiation between the parties. This is mainly reflected in the fact that in this case, Xiajiajie Coal Mine objectively could not adopt the usual practice of changing the mining right holder only after full payment or most of the payment had been made, in order to avoid the commercial risk that the mining right involved in the case would be changed to the name of the transferee while the transferor could not receive the transfer price. Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company successively signed four agreements regarding the transfer of the mining right involved in the case. The transfer prices, transfer times, and change times of the mining license reflected in the four agreements were inconsistent. Regarding the transfer price, the "Mining Right Equity Transfer Contract" and the "Supplemental Agreement" stipulated 30 million yuan and 38 million yuan respectively, while the "Mining Right Transfer Contract" filed and archived on the official website of the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources stipulated 7 million yuan. Xiajiajie Coal Mine claimed that the reason Jiashenglong Company was able to change the registration of the mining right involved in the case to its name after paying only a deposit of 1 million yuan was because it was done in accordance with the requirements of the Guizhou Province coal mine enterprise merger and reorganization policy. The "Guizhou Province Coal Mine Enterprise Merger and Reorganization Work Plan (Trial)" (Qian Fu Ban [2012] No. 61) issued by the General Office of the Guizhou Provincial People's Government, which states that merger and reorganization work should be basically completed by March 31, 2014, and that all types of certificates and licenses of coal mines after merger and reorganization must be changed to the name of the merger and reorganization entity, can corroborate Xiajiajie Coal Mine's above claim. Therefore, the change of the mining right involved in the case to the name of Jiashenglong Company on November 20, 2013, was not the true intention of Xiajiajie Coal Mine.

Second, Jiashenglong Company recognized that Xiajiajie Coal Mine is the actual right holder of the mining right involved in the case. The agreement in the "Agreement" signed by Jiashenglong Company and Xiajiajie Coal Mine that "the 'Mining Right Transfer Contract' signed as required by the Provincial Department of Land and Resources is only used for handling the merger and reorganization of the coal mine mining right and shall not serve as the true basis for payment of the mining right transaction," and the "Confirmation of Property Rights" issued by Jiashenglong Company, both reflect that Jiashenglong Company also confirmed that it had not paid the transfer price for the mining right involved in the case as agreed, and that the mining right involved in the case still belonged to Xiajiajie Coal Mine.

Third, the local administrative department recognized that the merger and reorganization of Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company had not been completed, and had conducted mediation regarding the property rights exit compensation. From the "Statement" confirmed by the Emergency Management Bureau of Libo County, the district where the coal mine involved in the case is located, it appears that the relevant administrative department conducted mediation regarding the property rights exit compensation between the two parties, and the local administrative department was aware of the merger and reorganization situation between the two parties.

Fourth, Jiashenglong Company did not actually operate the coal mine involved in the case. After the registration of the mining right involved in the case was changed to the name of Jiashenglong Company, the coal mine involved in the case was closed as required by the relevant policies of Guizhou Province on coal mine enterprise merger and reorganization, and no substantive merger and reorganization has occurred. Although Jiashenglong Company is the registered right holder, apart from being a nominal holder, it did not actually operate the mining right involved in the case or the coal mine involved in the case.

In summary, the mining right involved in the case was formally changed and registered in the name of Jiashenglong Company in accordance with the requirements of the Guizhou Province coal mine enterprise merger and reorganization policy. Jiashenglong Company did not actually operate and derive benefits. Therefore, it should be determined that Xiajiajie Coal Mine is the actual right holder of the mining right involved in the case.

II. Whether the civil right and interest of Xiajiajie Coal Mine in the mining right involved in the case is sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement in this case

This court holds that, as the actual right holder of the mining right involved in the case, the civil right and interest of Xiajiajie Coal Mine in the mining right involved in the case is sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement in this case. The reasons are as follows:

On the one hand, there is no situation in this case where the actual right holder needs to yield to a priority right. The seizure of the mining right involved in this case was based on an effective judgment in the private lending dispute case between Zhang Xuexin and Jiashenglong Company. Zhang Xuexin holds an ordinary monetary creditor's right against Jiashenglong Company based on that effective judgment, and Zhang Xuexin did not create a security interest in the mining right involved in the case. There is also no situation in this case involving priority rights such as the right to be compensated from construction project proceeds or the right of habitation.

On the other hand, when Zhang Xuexin provided the loan to Jiashenglong Company, the mining right involved in the case was not registered in the name of Jiashenglong Company. The creditor's right that Zhang Xuexin sought to enforce arose from September to October 2013, at which time the mining right involved in the case had not yet been changed and registered in the name of Jiashenglong Company. When providing the loan to Jiashenglong Company, Zhang Xuexin did not check the status of the mining rights under Jiashenglong Company's name. The information that the mining right involved in the case had no mortgage or the like was discovered by the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court during the enforcement procedure through inquiry to the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources. Zhang Xuexin's provision of the loan to Jiashenglong Company was not influenced by the mining right involved in the case. Furthermore, based on the facts found by this court, Zhang Xuexin was aware of the Guizhou Province coal mine enterprise merger and reorganization policy, and was authorized to exercise on behalf of Jiashenglong Company all rights enjoyed by the acquired coal mine's investor. The use of funds in the two bank accounts opened by Jiashenglong Company for the merger and reorganization required Zhang Xuexin's consent. From this, it can be seen that Zhang Xuexin should have been aware of the merger and reorganization transaction between Jiashenglong Company and Xiajiajie Coal Mine, the payment status of the transfer price, and that Xiajiajie Coal Mine was the actual right holder.

The judgment of second instance held that "the mining right is a特许 right to exploit mineral resources obtained upon administrative examination and approval, which is different from ordinary real rights. The claim of Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company that the mining right of the mine is an affiliation relationship and that Xiajiajie Coal Mine remains the actual mining right holder of the mine involved in the case lacks legal basis and cannot negate the mining license lawfully issued by the administrative authority to Jiashenglong Company." The judgment of second instance essentially determined the right holder of the mining right involved in the case strictly according to the administrative licensing registration. This concerns the public trust effect of the administrative licensing registration of the mining right. The public trust effect of real right registration is the legal effect of the real right publicity system. The so-called public trust effect means that the registered right holder of the mining right is legally presumed to be the true right holder. For a person who has engaged in a transaction relying on such registration, even if the registration is later proven to be erroneous, the law still recognizes the same legal effect as a true mining right, in order to protect the reliance interest of a third party who transacted based on the registered content. However, between the registered right holder and the interested party, the presumption effect of public notice and public trust does not apply. In this case, Zhang Xuexin was aware of the Guizhou Province coal mine enterprise merger and reorganization policy, and was authorized to exercise on behalf of Jiashenglong Company all rights enjoyed by the acquired coal mine's investor. Zhang Xuexin should have been aware that the registration of the mining right involved in the case in the name of Jiashenglong Company was carried out in accordance with the merger and reorganization policy requirements, and that Jiashenglong Company only paid a deposit of 1 million yuan. Under these circumstances, Zhang Xuexin is not a third party who was completely unaware of the merger and reorganization transaction between Xiajiajie Coal Mine and Jiashenglong Company, or that Xiajiajie Coal Mine was the actual right holder of the mining right involved in the case. Therefore, the registration of the mining right involved in the case in the name of Jiashenglong Company does not raise the issue of protecting reliance interests with respect to Zhang Xuexin.

Furthermore, Zhang Xuexin argued that before this court ruled to bring the case up for retrial, the mining right involved in the case had already been transferred to a person not involved in the case through the enforcement procedure, and therefore Xiajiajie Coal Mine no longer had a litigious interest. In this regard, this court holds that in this case, the enforcement court issued the Enforcement Ruling (2019) Qian 27 Zhi Hui No. 9-Zhi 5, which transferred the mining right involved in the case to satisfy a debt by reason of the failed auction. This was not an execution through auction or sale and transfer to a person not involved in the case; rather, it should be regarded as a ruling for debt satisfaction by property transfer made by the people's court during the enforcement procedure. Paragraph 2 of Article 6 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Execution Objection and Reconsideration Cases by People's Courts" provides: "If a person not involved in the case raises an objection in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law, it shall be raised before the execution of the subject matter of the objection is completed; if the subject matter of execution is transferred to a party, the objection shall be raised before the enforcement procedure is completed." The filing of this lawsuit by Xiajiajie Coal Mine complies with the above legal provisions. Although the mining right involved in the case was transferred to Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine by a ruling for debt satisfaction by property transfer, Xiajiajie Coal Mine had the right to file an execution objection to protect its lawful rights and interests after the seizure of the subject matter of execution and before the conclusion of the enforcement procedure. In addition, although the Enforcement Ruling (2019) Qian 27 Zhi Hui No. 9-Zhi 5 confirmed the delivery of the mining right involved in the case to Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine, this ruling is a ruling for debt satisfaction by property transfer made by the people's court during the enforcement procedure. Transferring the registration of the mining right involved in the case to the name of Panxian Xinmin Fuxin Coal Mine does not involve issues such as maintaining the stability of judicial auction and sale procedures or protecting the interests of unspecified third parties. The scope of non-execution in the judgment of this case may extend to this ruling.

In summary, Xiajiajie Coal Mine has a civil right and interest in the mining right involved in the case sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement. Item 1 of Paragraph 1 of Article 312 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" provides that if the person not involved in the case has a civil right and interest in the subject matter of execution sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement, a judgment shall be rendered not to enforce the subject matter of execution. This case shall be adjudicated that the mining right involved in the case shall not be enforced. Paragraph 1 of Article 314 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: "With respect to an action for execution objection by a person not involved in the case, if the people's court renders a judgment not to enforce the subject matter of execution, the execution objection ruling becomes void." After this judgment takes effect, the Enforcement Ruling (2019) Qian 27 Zhi Yi No. 54 of the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court shall become invalid, and there is no need for this court to revoke that ruling in the judgment items. For the reasons stated above, the ruling for debt satisfaction by property transfer made during the enforcement procedure regarding the mining right involved in the case, i.e., the Enforcement Ruling (2019) Qian 27 Zhi Hui No. 9-Zhi 5 of the Qiannan Prefecture Intermediate People's Court, should also be revoked, and enforcement measures such as seizure shall be lifted.

To sum up, the retrial claims of Xiajiajie Coal Mine are established. Pursuant to Article 207, Paragraph 1 and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Revoke the Civil Judgment (2020) Qian Min Zhong No. 476 of the Guizhou High People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2019) Qian 27 Min Chu No. 122 of the Qiannan Buyi and Miao Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court;

2. The mining right (Certificate No. C5200002012011120122487) of Xiajiajie Coal Mine, Maolan Town, Libo County, of Guizhou Jiashenglong Group Mining Investment Co., Ltd. shall not be enforced.

Court acceptance fee of 60,800 yuan for first instance and court acceptance fee of 60,800 yuan for second instance shall be borne by Zhang Xuexin.
